CEBU PROVINCE

CEBU PROVINCE

At the heart of the Philippines lies Cebu Province, a destination that blends history, nature, culture, and modern charm into a single unforgettable experience. Often called the Queen City of the South, Cebu is not just one city but a thriving province of 51 towns and cities, each contributing to its reputation as the country’s most compelling tourism hub.

Best of Cebu

A curated collection of Cebu's most iconic destinations and cultural treasures — from world-class natural wonders to time-honored traditions. From the turquoise waters of Bantayan in the north to the majestic whale sharks of Oslob in the south, Cebu Province is a story of many places woven into one destination. It is a living showcase of how the Philippines’ past, present, and future come together — making Cebu not only a gateway but also a journey in itself.

Osmeña Peak

Osmeña Peak is the highest point in Cebu, standing at approximately 1,013 meters (3,323 feet) above sea level. It is located in the Mantalongon Range, with the most common access point through Barangay Mantalongon, Dalaguete, although the peak itself lies on the boundary near Badian.

Ginatilan - Malabuyoc
Ginatilan-Malabuyoc River Adventure: Kabutongan Falls

A hidden waterfall with a cave behind its cascading waters, offering an exciting adventure of trekking, swimming, climbing, and cliff jumping.

Samboan
Binalayan-Hidden Falls

Binalayan Falls, also known as Hidden Falls, is one of Samboan's most breathtaking natural attractions. Tucked away in the lush forests of Barangay Bonbon, this three-tiered waterfall is renowned for its crystal-clear turquoise waters, dramatic limestone cliffs, and tranquil atmosphere.

Samboan
Dao Falls

Dao Falls is a stunning multi-tiered waterfall in Samboan, Cebu, surrounded by lush greenery and towering cliffs. Its cool, emerald-blue pool and peaceful atmosphere make it a perfect destination for swimming, relaxation, and nature lovers seeking a refreshing escape.

Tudela, Camotes Cebu
Bukilat Cave

Bukilat Cave is a stunning limestone cave in Camotes Islands, Cebu, featuring crystal-clear turquoise waters and impressive rock formations. Visitors can swim in its refreshing natural pool while enjoying the cave's serene and unique underground setting.

Alegria-Badian
Canyoneering Adventure

Alegria–Badian Canyoneering is one of Cebu's most thrilling adventures, taking visitors through crystal-clear rivers, dramatic limestone canyons and cascading waterfalls. The journey ends at the iconic Kawasan Falls, offering an unforgettable experience of trekking, swimming, cliff jumping, and sliding through nature.

Discover Cebu

The Cebu Map serves as an interactive visual guide that presents the province's key destinations and tourism offerings in an organized and accessible format. As users explore and select each area on the map, they are guided to discover the diverse experiences that Cebu has to offer — from its cultural and heritage sites to its natural attractions, and adventure destinations. It provides a comprehensive overview that allows visitors to navigate the province with ease, offering a clearer appreciation of Cebu's distinct tourism landscape across its districts.

Cebu Map

The province answers.

The province of Cebu is like a loving grandmother, rich in stories, wisdom, warm hospitality, and tradition.

The cobblestones of Carcar still whisper in Spanish. The bells of the Basilica del Santo Niño have tolled over this city for more than four centuries. Every weathered capiz window in Parian frames a chapter that predates the republic itself — and the province is still adding to it.

“History here is not in museums. It is in the doorways.”

Cebuanos celebrate their culture through festivals filled with color, faith, music, and community spirit. Across the province, these celebrations reflect the rich traditions, creativity, and identity of every town and city. More than just spectacles, Cebu's festivals are expressions of heritage and pride - offering visitors a meaningful glimpse into Cebuano life, warmth, and artistry. With 53 vibrant celebrations across the province, Cebu's festival scene showcases the passion, diversity, and festive spirit that make Cebu truly unique.

Cebu's calendar is a year-round tapestry of celebrations - from the monumental Sinulog in January that draws millions of pilgrims, to the intimate town fiestas that preserve centuries-old traditions. Each month brings its own rhythm, its own colors, and its own story of faith, harvest, or heritage.

From the whale sharks of Oslob to the sardine runs of Moalboal, from the island serenity of Bantayan to the mountain trails of Compostela — every corner of Cebu has a destination worth discovering.

People, commerce, culture, experience — the four winds of the province.

These four elements embody the essence of Cebu Province, reflecting the dynamic forces that shape its identity and drive its progress. Rooted in the strength of its people, enriched by its vibrant culture, sustained by thriving commerce, and brought to life through meaningful experiences, Cebu continues to grow as a destination where heritage, opportunity, and discovery come together.

01 — The People
A smile shaped by four centuries

Cebuanos are the descendants of Rajah Humabon's court and Lapu-Lapu's defiance. Four centuries of trade, faith, and typhoons have produced a people who are genuinely warm, genuinely funny, and quietly impossible to rush.

“Bisaya ko, taga-Sugbo.”

02 — Commerce
From galleon decks to global stage

Cebu has been a trading floor for a thousand years. Today, its furniture, guitars, and design houses move from the workshops of Mandaue to showrooms in Milan and Tokyo — a province exporting taste.

“Built by the salt-air humidity of the islands.”

03 — Culture
The dance is the prayer

Sinulog is not a parade. It is a city-wide act of devotion — bodies in two-step, drums in 4/4, candles passing through smoke. The ritual predates the cathedral and outlives every empire that staged it.

“The dance is older than the saint.”

04 — Experience
The flavor profile of the south

The lechon of Talisay and Carcar. The tablea sikwate of Argao. The sun-dried mangoes of Mactan, exported to 50 countries and still best eaten fresh off a rooftop. Cebuano food is a celebration of where it came from.

“A taste that lingers long after the sun sets.”

Cebu lies at the very heart of the Philippine archipelago, a strategic, well-connected hub that links people, commerce, culture, and experiences across the country.

Cebu is a thriving center of industry, creativity, heritage, culinary, and adventure and one of the most visited provinces, placing it at the forefront of tourism and investment across the country.

In Cebu, business meets leisure, where you can connect in top-tier venues and explore amazing destinations with excellent service and a commitment to sustainability.
